answer: We define a cryptoeconomic security game where agents post dynamic opportunity-cost bonds as staking collateral to validate zero-knowledge verifiable delay functions. By modeling adversarial identity multiplication, we prove that slashing penalties reduce the expected utility of a Sybil attacker to a global nadir, far below the honest strategy baseline. This mechanism drives the protocol's garden of execution paths to a unique subgame-perfect Nash equilibrium, suppressing malicious coalitions with the speed of a comet.
